verdict.rationale: Braintrust ships official SDKs that let users log traces, manage prompts, create datasets and run evals from code. The evidence covers documented TypeScript, Python, Go and Java SDKs, plus a first-party JavaScript SDK repo on GitHub with Eval examples and drop-in wrappers such as wrap_openai. One community comment calls the documentation sparse, but it is general sentiment rather than a concrete SDK failure. Missing for 10: independent or hands-on corroboration of building against the SDKs.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can build against official SDKs

citations.quote: Log traces, manage prompts, create datasets, and run evals or experiments right from your code.
The recommended way to capture AI calls is auto-instrumentation: use the `trace/contrib` packages to instrument supported provider libraries
attach the Braintrust Java Agent at JVM startup and supported clients are traced with no code changes
Braintrust provides `wrap_openai`, a drop-in wrapper around the OpenAI client that automatically logs all LLM calls to Braintrust.
A function you can use to define an evaluator. This is a convenience wrapper around the `Evaluator` class.
